Regenerate the mock owner public key and metric_{on,off} policies At some point, the acceptable format for the owner key changed, in terms of header sizes. This can be seen in commit d29ae33459d4 ("Updated policy_testserver to support verification key signatures"), in the chrome repo. Unfortunately, the code in this directory was not updated. As a result, if a user had logged into a test machine at any point before running platform_KernelErrorPaths (i.e. the machine has an owner), the test machine gets powerwashed and the test fails. The original code for generating the public key and the policy blobs is found attached to this document: https://sites.google.com/a/google.com/chromeos/archive/testing-tools-for-device-policies Along with it are the instructions to generate the keys. We follow these instructions and commit the updated code. TEST=platform_KernelErrorPaths.BUG passes after this. Tried running platform_KernelErrorPaths.ALL, but it has other issues. KernelErrorPaths: modify SysRQ-X test behaviour to match implementation Ever since the commit "CHROMIUM: sysrq: Stop trying to kill X server for 'X' key" sysrq-X can only be triggered twice in 20 seconds, before the machine reboots. Prior to that commit, sysrq-X would have to be triggered thrice, with the second instance killing the X server. The test continues to behave as if the old behaviour is in affect. This change modifies it to expect the new behaviour. BUG=chromium:966593 TEST=Ran platform_KernelErrorPaths.SYSRQ_X to make sure I didn't break anything else. But, I didn't reproduce this bug myself. crash: lock |core_pattern| once crash-reporter is initialized For kernels older that linux-4.4, lock_core_pattern was added to prevent modifications to the core_pattern once crash-repoter is done with initialization. This patch also adds code to handle failure to reset the core_pattern if it is locked: this can occur during "crash-reporter --clean_shutdown" on devices that support the core pattern lock. The locking of the core_pattern is conditional on the image type (disabled on dev images) to allow for a regression test in logging_UserCrash. BUG=chromium:960445 TEST=logging_UserCrash passes. autotest: Fix boot detection in logging and return result There was a bug introduced before where we no longer properly found the boot line when searching through log files. This was because the regex got changed to be a partial line match and the regex function was using 'match' instead of 'search'. power_WakeupRTC: Run test only on devices which are wakeup capable The test loops through all available RTC devices on the system and then runs the test on each of them. There might be cases where a device is not wakeup capable. For such cases the test would fail, which it should not. So run the test only on devices which are wakeup capable. Do this by looking for /sys/class/rtc/rtc<X>/device/power/wakeup file present or not. Also fail the test if /dev/rtc0 does not exist or does not have wakeup capability, since there are many things in the system which rely on /dev/rtc0 being present and have wakeup capability. lakitu: Remove checking of uid and gid to be same Recently, when update engine tries to update an instance from old COS image to newer COS image, update gets failed. This happens due to following reason: 1. When google-account-daemon tries to allocate UID and GID for users that have existing /home/<user> dir, it tries to use old UID and GID if old UID and GID were same. 2. Recently, a new user 'crash' had been added with UID and GID as 20137. So, after the update, when google-accounts-daemon tries to allocate UID and GID for existing users, it is not able to use the old UID and GID as they are not same which is a mandate for the associated patch.Thereby, it assigns a new UID and GID which is greater than 20137 (above exisiting highest UID). This results in bad ownership while doing ssh as the UID and GID associated with /home/<user> is different from UID and GID of user. CHROMIUM: scripts: change dm_verity alg to sha256 Change dm_verity hash algorithm fom sha1 to sha256. Due to collision attacks against SHA1 and increasing severity of collisions there is a need to change the hash algorithm to SHA256. BUG=chromium:719966 TEST=Bootperf tool is used to make the boot performance measurements. Boot time measurements taken from kernel start to login screen from high performance/ low power ARM and x86 platforms show that changing dm_verity hash algorithm from SHA1 to SHA256 has boot time changes less than 277 ms on chrome_main when the crypto accelerators(for ARM) and SSSE3(for x86) kernel configurations are enabled. The difference is less for higher kernel versions and newer CPUs. For new kernel versions and CPUs the changes even increase boot time performance upto 717 ms.. Results are on go/cros-boot-sha256. seccomp: Add a bunch of calls for mosys' children Mosys reaches out and executes a shell script, vpd_get_value. One example of its invocation is "/usr/local/sbin/vpd_get_value customization_id" This script reaches out in various cases and launches a bunch of different things. Examples include: /usr/sbin/vpd /usr/sbin/crossystem fmap-base /usr/sbin/dmidecode -s chassis-type /usr/sbin/dump_vpd_log Other programs such as sed, awk, mkdir, mktemp, mv, etc. I was noticing while staring at the logs to debug a different recovery issue that this was generating seccomp issues. It seems to come from: /usr/share/cros/cr50-set-board-id.sh check_device which is called by chromeos-install. Add the system calls needed to get this command to run without issue inside the /usb chroot during recovery. It's getting a little expensive to keep mosys working with seccomp. It would be better to see mosys stop executing random scripts it finds throughout the system. Making this visible was not easy. To test this on Hatch, I had to: * Edit ~/trunk/src/scripts/mod_image_for_recovery.sh to add --enable_serial=ttyS0 to the build_kernel_image.sh command line * Edit and cros_workon ~/trunk/src/platform/initramfs: * Add /usr/bin/strace to recovery/Makefile * Comment out the exec>"${LOG_FILE}" in recovery/init * Add /bin/sh -i into recovery/recovery_init.sh, just before running chromeos-recovery. * Manually add the equivalent of USE=pcserial to the kernel configs * emerge-hatch strace, the kernel, and initramfs. * Run build_image (with console enabled), mod_image_for_recovery.sh --board=hatch --image=chromiumos_test_image.bin, then boot into the new image. At the shell, you can run: chroot /usb /tmp/strace -f /usr/sbin/mosys platform brand And look for instances of SIGSYS happening in any of the output.
